question: A 39-year-old male presents to your office with nodular skin lesions that progress from his right hand to right shoulder. The patient reports that the initial lesion, currently necrotic and ulcerative, developed from an injury he received while weeding his shrubs a couple weeks earlier. The patient denies symptoms of respiratory or meningeal disease. Which of the following most likely characterizes the pattern of this patient’s skin lesions:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Traumatic injury -> Nodular skin lesions -> Progression from right hand to right shoulder -> 80% CHAIN: Necrotic and ulcerative lesion -> Initial lesion developed from an injury -> 85% CHAIN: No symptoms of respiratory or meningeal disease reported -> Unlikely to be hematogenous dissemination -> 90% CHAIN: Lesions progressing from a localized site -> Unlikely to be dermatophyte colonization -> 85% CHAIN: Lesions following a linear pattern -> Possible ascending lymphangitis -> 70% CHAIN: History of weeding shrubs -> Possible exposure to arthropods -> Possible arthropod bite -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with nodular skin lesions that are necrotic and ulcerative, following an initial injury, is most consistent with ascending lymphangitis. This condition typically presents with a linear pattern of nodular lesions that progress along lymphatic channels from the site of entry.
